headline_marked: BNP MP [[Ferdousi Ahmed Misty resigns]] after attack on health center
headline: BNP MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty resigns after attack on health center
summary: The resignation follows a directive from party chief Tarique Rahman, sending a strong message on accountability for those in power.
details: BNP's reserved seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty has resigned from her parliamentary seat following a directive from party chief Tarique Rahman.
The resignation comes after Misty was named in connection with attacks, looting, and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP health center in Mirpur, Dhaka.
Attorney General Md. Ruhul Quddus Kajal noted that the resignation sends a message that no one will be spared if allegations of wrongdoing are found, regardless of their position.
The Attorney General compared this to the case of Jamaat-e-Islami MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, who was expelled from his party but remains an MP because he did not resign.
According to the Attorney General, under Article 70 of the Constitution, a seat only becomes vacant if a member resigns or votes against their party in Parliament.
He stated that while Jamaat took organizational action, Tarique Rahman's decision led to an actual vacancy of the parliamentary seat, demonstrating a higher level of accountability.
The Election Commission has announced that a by-poll for the vacant reserved seat must be held within 90 days.
caption:
A BNP MP has resigned her seat after being linked to a health center attack. This move signals a strong shift in party accountability.

BNP's reserved seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty has resigned from her parliamentary seat following a directive from party chief Tarique Rahman.

The resignation comes after Misty was named in connection with attacks, looting, and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP health center in Mirpur, Dhaka.

Attorney General Md. Ruhul Quddus Kajal noted that the resignation sends a message that no one will be spared if allegations of wrongdoing are found, regardless of their position.

The Attorney General compared this to the case of Jamaat-e-Islami MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, who was expelled from his party but remains an MP because he did not resign.

According to the Attorney General, under Article 70 of the Constitution, a seat only becomes vacant if a member resigns or votes against their party in Parliament.

He stated that while Jamaat took organizational action, Tarique Rahman's decision led to an actual vacancy of the parliamentary seat, demonstrating a higher level of accountability.

The Election Commission has announced that a by-poll for the vacant reserved seat must be held within 90 days.

headline_marked: Expelled Jubo Dal leader [[taken into custody after Banglamotor altercation]]
headline: Expelled Jubo Dal leader taken into custody after Banglamotor altercation
summary: Ferdous Ahmed Simon was detained by police following an incident that left a man injured and sparked protests from locals over extortion allegations.
details: A 45-year-old man was injured during an altercation with Ferdous Ahmed Simon, an expelled convener of Hatirjheel Thana Jubo Dal, in Dhaka’s Banglamotor on Thursday night.

The incident occurred around 8:10 pm in a lane on the northern side of Banglamotor. According to Hatirjheel Police Station OC Md Asaduzzaman, the two men, who are neighbors, became involved in an argument.
The victim, Sohan, was struck on the head and sustained injuries. Police also received allegations that Simon fired two blank rounds at the scene, adding to the tension in the area.
Following the incident, more than 100 locals gathered outside Simon’s home, chanting slogans and accusing him of long-term extortion activities.
The situation escalated as a motorcycle was seen on fire beside the Banglamotor-Moghbazar road around 11:15 pm, requiring the intervention of the Fire Service.
Police and SRB personnel were deployed to manage the crowd, as some locals alleged that law enforcers were initially protecting Simon instead of detaining him.
Around midnight, police escorted Simon out of his residence and took him into custody. OC Asaduzzaman confirmed that legal proceedings are now underway.
caption:

A 45-year-old man was injured during an altercation with Ferdous Ahmed Simon, an expelled convener of Hatirjheel Thana Jubo Dal, in Dhaka’s Banglamotor on Thursday night.

The incident occurred around 8:10 pm in a lane on the northern side of Banglamotor. According to Hatirjheel Police Station OC Md Asaduzzaman, the two men, who are neighbors, became involved in an argument.

The victim, Sohan, was struck on the head and sustained injuries. Police also received allegations that Simon fired two blank rounds at the scene, adding to the tension in the area.

Following the incident, more than 100 locals gathered outside Simon’s home, chanting slogans and accusing him of long-term extortion activities.

The situation escalated as a motorcycle was seen on fire beside the Banglamotor-Moghbazar road around 11:15 pm, requiring the intervention of the Fire Service.
